Summary  
The source paper proposes a meta-gradient option-discovery method to speed up and generalise reinforcement-learning (RL) across multiple tasks. It frames the problem as discovering task-independent options through a manager-worker architecture whose option-reward and termination functions are optimised with meta-gradients. Experiments in Gridworld and DeepMind Lab show faster learning and improved transfer.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]  
The paper is short (extended abstract length). The causal-interventional chain is straight-forward, so confidence is high, though section titles are inferred (“Abstract”, “Method”, “Experiments”) because they are not included in the excerpt.  

Inference strategy justification  
Only light inference was used when explicit headings were absent and when mapping the method into an actionable intervention for the AI-safety lifecycle (Fine-Tuning/RL, maturity 2). All other elements were directly stated.  

Extraction completeness explanation  
All reasoning steps—risk (sample inefficiency, poor transfer) → problem cause (lack of temporal abstraction) → theoretical remedy (task-independent options) → design (manager-worker) → implementation (meta-gradient training) → validation (two empirical studies) → intervention—are captured. Nodes are uniquely named for cross-source merging, and every node participates in at least one edge, yielding a single connected fabric.  

Key limitations  
1. Section titles had to be inferred; real titles would strengthen traceability.  
2. The intervention’s lifecycle stage could arguably be 2 (pre-training) rather than 3; judgement was required.  
3. Only two validation nodes were created because the paper summarised two study suites; finer-grained metrics (e.g., learning-curve slopes) were unavailable in the excerpt.
